body:
## Problem

The v0.77.0 client-management commands exist, but a normal macOS workstation cannot use them as shipped:

- release assets contain only `linux-amd64` and `linux-arm64`; there is no Darwin binary;
- running the Linux binary in Docker cannot launch host-installed TUI/CLI programs for `with`, and mounting user configuration into Docker is not an acceptable substitute for a native isolated launcher;
- `clients setup --token` has no `--token-stdin` or documented token environment variable, so configuring an existing remote-router JWT requires putting it in argv/shell history/process listings;
- the command has no explicit config-root/home option, which makes isolated automation and acceptance tests awkward and encourages mounting a real home directory.

## Expected behavior

- Publish signed/checksummed native binaries for Darwin arm64 and amd64 alongside Linux assets (and document a supported install/update path).
- `clients setup`, `show`, `doctor`, `remove`, and `with` work natively on macOS for every supported client.
- Add `--token-stdin` and a documented environment variable for existing router tokens; redact secrets from diagnostics.
- Add an explicit isolated config/home option so automation can prove setup → doctor → launch → remove without touching real user settings.
- Add release tests on macOS that run the actual host CLI integration lifecycle against a remote Router URL through an SSH-forwarded localhost port.

This is required for the client configuration feature to be usable where Codex, Claude Code, Gemini, Qwen, Grok, OpenCode, Cursor, and Agent are commonly installed.
title: Make client setup usable on macOS and secret-safe for remote routers
